extracted.intended_audience: theater practitioners, directors, teachers, actors, and improvisation students
extracted.subtask_description: A publications/catalog page describing Viola Spolin's books and the practical improvisational/theater-game techniques they teach for directors, actors (including solo performers), and classroom instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artistic aim: go beyond what we already know
rubrics_metrics.description: “In any art form we seek the experience of going beyond what we already know.” — Viola Spolin
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the desired outcome of improvisational practice: facilitating experiences that expand performers' existing knowledge/abilities. Use as a high-level evaluative yardstick for exercises, games, or techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad applicability of techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Viola Spolin's improvisational techniques changed the very nature and practice of modern theater... These techniques have also influenced the fields of education, mental health, social work, and psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for judging techniques or materials: they should be adaptable beyond stage performance to related fields (education, therapy, social work, media). Materials that demonstrate cross-disciplinary usefulness score higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical rehearsal guidance for directors
rubrics_metrics.description: Theater Games for Rehearsal: A Director’s Handbook is a practical application of Viola Spolin’s method that guides directors and their companies step-by-step through all phases of the rehearsal period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Desired features: step-by-step procedures covering selecting plays/material, casting, building a harmonious company, warming up actors, creating stage space, and overcoming opening night jitters. Evaluative focus on clarity, completeness, and direct applicability to rehearsal workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo-actor exercises and side-coaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Theater Games for the Lone Actor offers theater games and side coaching for the solo player... more than forty exercises that allow actors to side coach themselves at home, in rehearsal, or in performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials should enable solo performers to self-coach: include exercises suitable for individual practice, clear instructions for self-guidance, and applicability in home, rehearsal, and performance contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive classroom instruction and age-range suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Theater Games For the Classroom... offers the most comprehensive theater instruction for all types of students, from small children to young adults. It includes over 130 theater games, plus exercises and instructional strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate classroom resources for breadth (number of games/exercises), explicit instructional strategies, and adaptability across age groups and skill levels. Resources that are usable with children through young adults and include teaching strategies rate highly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular, no-training-required classroom materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Theater Game File: a special selection of theater games, presented on separate cards in a convenient file box as self-contained classroom workshops... teachers and students alike, with no prior training or theater experience, can play theater games in the classroom with benefit to all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: materials packaged as self-contained, modular units (e.g., cards/workshops) that allow teachers with no theatrical background to run activities easily. Assess usability, modularity, and clarity of instructions for novices.
